findings.title: Async legacy write derives from request context that is cancelled when the request returns
findings.body: Each goroutine builds its timeout context from the request ctx. The apiserver cancels that ctx as soon as the handler returns, which happens right after the goroutine is launched. The legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection therefore often runs with an already-cancelled context and fails, so legacy storage silently stops being written. Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a background context that carries the needed values.

findings.title: Storage failure recorded as legacy duration
findings.body: In Create, a failure of the Storage write is recorded with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration. Update has the same mistake at line 129. As a result, failures of the unified store show up under the legacy metric.

findings.title: Name passed as kind label in Delete metric
findings.body: recordStorageDuration is called with `name` where `options.Kind` should be. This mislabels the metric and creates one label value per object name, giving unbounded metric cardinality.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage duration
findings.body: The async legacy DeleteCollection call records its result with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration. Legacy deletecollection results are therefore counted under the unified-storage metric.

findings.title: Delete context uses base logger without request fields
findings.body: In Delete, the context is built with klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) rather than the `log` built just above it. Downstream logs lose the name, kind and method fields.

findings.title: Legacy async errors are not logged and goroutines race with test mocks
findings.body: Errors from the background legacy writes are only counted in metrics and never logged, so divergence between the stores is hard to diagnose. In the unit tests, Delete and DeleteCollection set no legacy mock expectations. The goroutine then calls an unexpected mock method, which panics or races with test completion. The tests also never assert that the legacy write happened.

findings.title: Create error case does not exercise a storage failure
findings.body: The failing case only sets up a legacy expectation. The storage mock's Create has no expectation, so the test passes or fails based on mock behaviour rather than on a configured storage error.
